//: Pi settings drop-in for the artifact-first skill suite. Skills load via the Agent Skills standard (name+description at startup, body on demand, /skill:<name> to invoke). Extension packages are TypeScript, loaded by Pi via jiti (no build step). Paths resolve relative to the agent directory (~/.pi/agent) so the setup is machine-portable: scripts/install-pi-extensions.sh populates packages/pi-extensions at the pinned upstream revision.

subagents.//: explore is read-only by allowlist; grant it extra READ-ONLY tools here. This example grants the lsp navigation set. general gets every discovered tool automatically; add names to excludeExtraTools to take some away. Custom subagent types live as definition files under agents/ (implementer, tester, reviewer, merger, and researcher today — read fresh at each launch from the pinned Subagents Extension): the frontmatter carries name, description, exact provider/model, and optional skills preloading, tools allowlist, or disallowedTools denials (tool names must exist in the session, and the extension's fixed launcher exclusions always apply), and because custom types have no per-type settings yet they resolve effort from the shared thinkingLevel below (the per-type levels for explore and general are unchanged and keep short-circuiting it). Write, shell, and commit boundaries are enforced through frontmatter allow/deny lists plus prompt constraints, not per-path guarantees; runtime enforcement is unverified. Every subagent stays at or below medium effort using a supported provider-specific effort level; provider ladders differ, and GLM-5.3-Flash has no medium rung, so it runs at the verified low effort. If a configured model is unavailable or its effort ceiling cannot be verified, report it, fall back to a verified compatible model and effort, and ask the user when no verified fallback exists. Availability and runtime behavior are not asserted by this file; the local catalog is a cache, not live availability. The custom researcher definition deliberately reuses the type name the extension retired for its old built-in web researcher — exact custom matches resolve first, so the name maps to this definition, not to the retired mapping. The researcher definition uses an explicit tools allowlist (reads, web lookups, write, edit, bash) so its surface stays that named set instead of silently inheriting tools that appear later; reviewer and tester instead name disallowedTools and inherit everything else. An older comment described researcher as a built-in that no longer exists at the pinned revision; the custom definition replaces it.

statusline.//: Absolute degradation budget: at-or-over the effective limit = caveman. Thresholds are fractions of the limit. Env EFFECTIVE_LIMIT / Z_* override.

compaction.//: Native fixed-token auto-compaction is off; packages/model-compaction is the sole automatic trigger (50% of the active model's advertised window). keepRecentTokens is the 8k recent-context budget retained by both manual /compact and extension-triggered compaction. The fixed 200k Dumb-zone contract lives in `statusline`, not here.

modelPresets.//: Coding preset set: gpt-6-sol, glm-5.3-flash, kimi-reviewer. See packages/model-presets/ for the catalog parser and activation flow.

lsp.//: Add or override language servers without touching the Extension package dir; merged over the shipped servers.json. Example: "zig": { "cmd": "zls", "args": [], "extensions": [".zig"] }
